extracted.intended_audience: federal audit organizations, agency auditors, inspectors general, and agency management responsible for audit programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance summarizing major revisions to OMB Circular A-73 (Audit of Federal Operations and Programs), specifying organizational, procedural, and substantive requirements federal audit organizations must follow when planning, performing, coordinating, and following up audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and staffing reporting lines
rubrics_metrics.description: The section on Organization and staffing has been changed to parallel some of the requirements contained in the Inspectors General legislation. For example, the Circular now requires non-statutory audit organizations to report to the head or deputy head of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit organizations (including non-statutory ones) must have reporting relationships that ensure appropriate independence and visibility by reporting to the agency head or deputy head. The revision aligns organizational/reporting requirements with Inspectors General legislation to promote accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with followup, investigative, and management review units
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific references are now made to coordination between the audit organization, the designated followup official, investigative units, and other management review activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit work must be coordinated with the agency's designated followup official, investigative units, and other management review activities to avoid duplication, ensure proper handling of findings, and support timely followup and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training of professional audit staff
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to the need for adequate training of the professional staff was inserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit organizations are required to ensure professional staff receive adequate training. Training is a standing expectation to maintain audit quality and keep auditors current with standards, techniques, and relevant regulatory changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain records of the audit universe
rubrics_metrics.description: A new section was added to clarify the requirement for each audit organization to maintain records of its audit universe which identifies the organizations, programs, activities, and functions subject to audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit organizations must keep and update an 'audit universe' inventory that lists all entities, programs, activities, and functions that could be audited. This record underpins risk assessment, planning, and prioritization of audit resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for determining audit priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The section on establishing criteria for determining audit priorities has been amended to include reference to the vulnerability assessments and internal control reviews required by Circular A-123; the criteria was reordered and clarified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit priority-setting must explicitly consider vulnerability assessments and internal control reviews (per Circular A-123). Criteria should be clear, ordered, and documented to support why certain programs/activities are selected for audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on non-federal audits and recipient responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The section on reliance on non-federal audits was revised to reflect the responsibility of recipient organizations to arrange for audits of federally assisted programs as required by OMB Circulars A-102 (single audit concept), A-110, and the authorizing statutes and regulations for block grant programs. The responsibility of federal audit organizations for auditing these programs was revised accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When federally assisted programs are subject to non-federal (recipient) audits, audit organizations must account for recipient audit responsibilities and applicable OMB circulars. Federal auditors should determine appropriate reliance on such audits and clarify which audit responsibilities remain with federal audit organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of annual audit plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The section on preparation of annual audit plans has been revised and clarified to require specific data on the programs and operations which have been selected for audit. Also, a requirement that the plan be reviewed with the head or deputy head of the agency has been added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual audit plans must include specific data about selected programs and operations (e.g., scope, objectives, rationale). Plans must be reviewed with the agency head or deputy head to ensure alignment with agency priorities and oversight expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination of audit work across forums and councils
rubrics_metrics.description: The section on coordination of audit work has been changed and new paragraphs have been added describing the respective roles in the audit process of the President's Council on Integrity and Efficiency and the National and Regional Intergovernmental Audit Forums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit organizations should follow clarified roles and coordination mechanisms involving the President's Council on Integrity and Efficiency (PCIE) and National/Regional Intergovernmental Audit Forums to promote interagency coordination, share information, and reduce duplicated effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit followup and management action on recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The section on audit followup ... has been completely revised. Policies for audit followup are now set forth in Circular A-50, 'Audit followup.' This section now restates the importance of management action on audit recommendations and references Circular A-50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit organizations must implement followup procedures in line with Circular A-50, emphasizing management's responsibility to act on audit recommendations. The guideline stresses formal followup processes and coordination with designated followup officials.
